searchText: Excuse my uninformed question. But what is proof of custody? And how does this relate Ethereum? This is the first time I’ve heard about it. I only vaguely remember reading about it in the context of shards and CL having proof you have the data of a shard proof of custody is a crypto-economic commitment taht you have the data you are claiming exists and is valid This is used in sharding for committee members claim on data but you can use it on a (large) execution trace as well to prove that you did execution locally (assuming you make hte execution trace too large to reasonably (or cheaply) get from an external party here is the latest PoC construction for shard data https://ethresear.ch/t/a-0-001-bit-proof-of-custody/7409 Are we going to require that EL maintains those proofs of execution post merge + short time? maintaining isn't important in this context it is in shard data so there wouldn't be the random challenges just the bit on the comptuation which could be checked and fraud-proved by anyone I guess I am not clear on why execution can’t be outsourced? If the proof of custody is on the CL shards themselves? there are two proposed PoCs one would be on shard data one would be on execution the former ensures that you actually downloaded and stored the shard data the latter ensures taht you actually computed the EL execution yourself rather than just lazily voting 👍 without actually having a local EL doing the work both help solve "lazy validator" problems in different domains Thank you for explaining it like that 🙂 no more questions
